title: Using Data Mining and Machine Learning for Knowledge Discovery in Publications on Information Management and Data Insights
content: In an era of growing data volumes, advances in data storage and processing technologies have created a landscape in which organizations — whether commercial, government, or educational — increasingly request analytical methods that convert raw data into valuable, actionable insights and knowledge. This research employed Data Mining (DM) techniques — including text mining and social network analysis — and Machine Learning (ML) methods, specifically hierarchical agglomerative and K-means clustering, and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) for topic modeling, to support knowledge discovery across 287 scientific publications focused on information management and data insights. Main findings include: artificial intelligence and machine learning were the most common bigrams in titles; five clusters were identified, with cluster C1 containing the five most cited articles; LDA modeling identified six topics, with Topic 6, Machine Learning/Deep Learning and Predictive Modeling, containing 59 articles on technical and algorithmic aspects. This work could motivate researchers in Data, Information, and Management to deepen their understanding of the field, guide strategic academic development, and promote new knowledge and scientific advances within the discipline.
